tagline: Inland from the Guilford green on the 1824 turnpike.
intro: Route 77 starts at the Guilford green, goes round its west side, crosses US 1 and I-95, and heads inland as Durham Road through North Guilford, past Lake Quonnipaug and the Route 80 junction, into Durham. There it meets Route 17 just south of the town center, and the scenic road follows Route 17 on through.

It was chartered in 1824 as the Guilford and Durham Turnpike. Durham is a former farming village on the Coginchaug River with the trap rock of the Metacomet Ridge along its west side, and on the last full weekend of September it holds a fair run entirely by volunteers, where oxen, draft horses and tractors pull concrete weights.

moments.title: Lake Quonnipaug
moments.text: The road passes Guilford's largest lake, where a town park keeps a supervised beach and the water is open for swimming, paddling and fishing.

moments.title: Durham
moments.text: The town started one of the first public libraries in the country in 1733, two years after Benjamin Franklin started his in Philadelphia.
